senses.definition: The name of the Latin script letter Œ/œ..

quotes.text: […] that he was of a doughty and ethel stirp. His ayle and eam had both been bellipotent; […]
quotes.reference: 1856, Samuel Klinefelter Hoshour, Letters to Squire Pedant, in the East, page 33:

quotes.text: The violation of an ethel born or noble woman was paid for by a higher murde than that of an un-ethel or common person. The murder of all persons was in like manner paid for by a were or were-geld, nicely adjusted to their relative rank.
quotes.reference: 1861, Henry Brougham, The British Constitution: Its History, Structure, and Working, page 140:

quotes.text: "I have come to seek your counsel in your most ethel of ethical capacities. My problem is wholly mechanical."

examples: For quotations using this term, see Citations:ethel.
